period: first use claimed 1967; renamed/marketed as Fuzzz Boxx by 1968 in Sam Ash historical account
evidence_summary: Sam Ash's 2014 trademark publication states first use and first use in commerce of SAM ASH FUZZZ BOXX on 1967-12-31, while Sam Ash's own historical article says the house brand was originally the Astrotone in 1967 and describes a 1968 renaming. The two dates are preserved as a source conflict rather than collapsed into one chronology.

Fuzzboxes documents the earliest known Astrotone example as February 1967 and later surviving date-coded examples into 1969. Astro Amp service literature identifies Universal Amplifier Corp. at 615 West 131st Street, New York City.

A 1967 Sam Ash unit is documented alongside a March 1967 Astrotone example with matching board and component family, establishing concurrent production of the Sam Ash-labeled state and the Astro-branded state. Exact first retail date remains separate from the documented production state.

Tone Machines documents an extremely rare Sam Ash Fuzz-Stainer specimen and explicitly treats its origin as uncertain. Similar enclosure, wiring, switch style, and a board marking interpreted as SA-FZ suggest a Sam Ash-branded product, but available evidence does not establish Universal Amplifier manufacture or whether it may have been employee-built or a kit-related product.

Surviving Astrotone/Fuzzz Boxx examples show multiple production states, including phenolic and later green printed circuit boards and differing transistor generations. These are retained as period revisions under the same confirmed manufacturer unless independent evidence establishes a factory change.
